conventions.convention: Affine invariant theory is over C, with reduced finite-type classical varieties allowing empty and reducible spaces. Spec of a reduced finitely generated complex algebra denotes its complex closed-point variety in the classical quotient statements.

Unipotence means every nonzero finite-dimensional rational module has a nonzero fixed vector; reductivity excludes nontrivial closed normal unipotent subgroups. The reductive/linearly reductive equivalence is restricted to C.
Affine stability requires both a closed orbit in the whole affine variety and a finite stabilizer.
A linearization is supplied data. Its cocycle maps L at ghx to L at x, and twisting multiplies the fibre action by the character.
Good-quotient affineness, surjectivity and sheaf clauses concern associated schemes; the additional geometric fibre condition concerns complex closed points.
Projective semistability uses invariant sections of any positive tensor power. Stability adds finite stabilizer and closedness of the orbit inside the semistable locus.
The degree-one-generation bound is d=kL, with L the lcm of generator degrees and k=max(1,N-1); an arbitrary common multiple is not asserted sufficient.

Fppf covers are jointly surjective set-indexed families of flat locally finitely presented maps. The empty covering is allowed precisely for an empty target; a sheaf consequently has a singleton value there.
Groupoid composition means the second arrow first, then the first; the relation embedding is (target,source), and an equivalence relation requires a monomorphism on all test schemes.

Polynomial factorization augmentations need not be surjective. The bounded factorization category is opposite to the polynomial-presentation category, and the cotangent diagram is contravariant on it.
Normalization is the intersection of kernels of faces i<n, with differential (-1)^n d_n. The ordinary cotangent complex uses cohomological degree -n for simplicial degree n.

Resolution comparison assumes polynomial resolutions with trivial Kan augmentations. Ordinary-ring base change is an isomorphism only under the stated derived-pushout, equivalently Tor-independence, condition.
Dold–Kan concerns constant coefficient rings. Variable simplicial modules use their separate model structures; diagram models are strict and do not assert coherent-diagram strictification.
Fixed-base derived derivations keep the simplicial base A and augmentation target B fixed; weak replacement of these bases is a separate interface.

The discrete-scheme inclusion has truncation as right adjoint. The full derived structure module is distinguished from its derived pullback to truncation; global homotopical gluing is imported from the named sources.
Choice assumptions are explicit in the reductive bridge, quotient, descent, sheafification and derived-comparison results; their elementary computations do not remove inherited assumptions.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC, a complex reductive affine algebraic group has completely reducible finite-dimensional rational modules. Every rational module is a direct sum of simples, with a unique stable complement to its invariants and a natural Reynolds projection; surjections remain surjective on invariants. On rational commutative algebras the projection is linear over invariants. Haar averaging and the convex-hull characterization are conditional on a compact Zariski-dense subgroup being supplied.

Under AC, for an affine algebraic set with an algebraic action of a complex reductive affine group, invariants are finitely generated; generators give a closed image canonically representing them; the resulting surjective map is categorical for classical-variety targets. Closed invariant subsets induce closed quotient immersions, images preserve intersections, and every fibre contains exactly one closed orbit. Irreducibility descends, and normality descends when X is also irreducible.

Under AC, simplicial modules and commutative unital or nonunital algebras over any simplicial commutative unital ring admit functorial model structures: weak equivalences are normalized additive quasi-isomorphisms, fibrations have underlying horn lifting, and cofibrations lift against underlying boundary-lifting maps. Free boundaries and horns generate the classes; the simplicial corner and inherited slice assertions hold. No properness or tensor-flatness is asserted.

Under AC, polynomial simplicial A-algebra resolutions of ordinary B with trivial Kan augmentations compute canonically isomorphic cotangent complexes in D(B). Any ordinary ring square induces the derived coefficient comparison; it is an isomorphism when B tensor-derived over A with A' maps quasi-isomorphically to B'. For an ordinary pushout this is the vanishing of all positive Tor groups; flat base change suffices.
Under AC, descent data for schemes over an fppf covering are effective when all structure morphisms are separated and locally quasi-finite; the descended scheme has both properties.
Under AC, the fppf quotient sheaf of a scheme by an etale equivalence relation is an algebraic space, and its quotient map is etale and surjective, giving a presentation.

Under AC, a complex reductive affine group acting on a complex projective variety with a supplied ample linearized invertible sheaf has a finitely generated invariant section ring and projective finite-type Proj quotient. Invariant affine charts cover the open semistable locus and glue to a good quotient. Positive tensor powers preserve both loci and quotient data, and compatible equivariant embeddings recover the ambient linear-action semistable and stable loci.

For a constant commutative unital ring R, normalization with differential (-1)^n d_n is an exact equivalence between simplicial R-modules and nonnegative chain complexes, with the stated surjection-indexed direct-sum inverse. No AC is needed; variable simplicial coefficient rings are excluded from this identification.

Under AC, contravariant module diagrams on a small category form an abelian category with pointwise exactness, projective free representables and enough projectives. Bounded-above derived colimits exist; a degree-zero diagram is computed by the bar complex whose coefficient-end face uses restriction.

Under AC and for fixed simplicial A and A-algebra B, a free-cell cofibrant replacement P over B gives Q ker(B tensor over A P to B), naturally B tensor over P Ω(P/A), representing relative derived derivations in the supplied enriched model. It is replacement-independent for this fixed augmented object and agrees with the ordinary cotangent complex for constant ordinary rings.

alerts.finding: F2 says the Lichtenbaum–Schlessinger complex 'admits a canonical map L_{B/A} to L_• in D(B) inducing an isomorphism τ≥−2 L_{B/A} to L_•', but attaches citations to def-cotangent-complex-of-a-ring-map, lem-cotangent-complex-resolution-independence and def-standard-resolution-of-a-ring-map. Those opened suppliers construct and compare polynomial-resolution cotangent complexes; they do not state the Lichtenbaum–Schlessinger comparison. Proof 1.2 separately cites the matching [Stacks Lemma 92.13.3, tag 09CG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09CG), whose statement and complete printed proof were opened. The concern is the attribution in F2, not a counterexample to the comparison.

seams_checked.note: The stabilizer and translated-fibre uses preserve finite type, separated target and rational-point hypotheses. The connected orbit supplier is applied only after smoothness and connectedness are supplied; locally closed irreducible orbits are explicitly established in its Proof 1.1. The owned lemma separately proves the disconnected-group extension.

The field-level quotient-sheaf use in cex-quotient-stack-need-not-be-a-scheme matches the opened sheafification convention. For the trivial action on Spec k the naive quotient is already terminal and a sheaf; no scheme representability theorem for arbitrary actions is inferred.

The five direct citing items were opened. Ordinary-ring domains, cohomological degrees, H0/polynomial cases and the Tor-independent base-change condition are preserved. The exception is lem-lichtenbaum-schlessinger-complex-and-cotangent-ext F2: it attributes the stronger Lichtenbaum–Schlessinger truncation comparison to resolution suppliers that do not state it. Its proof separately cites the exact Stacks theorem; the presentation alert records this limited mismatch.
